body:
I confirmed that I could reproduce the bug using the MRP in each of the 5 linked issues (#119740, #119752, #89657, #95512, #87626) in the latest master (af481fd223, so including the "Do not inline new operators" fix) with `g++ (GCC) 16.2.1 20260810` built with `scons production=yes optimize=speed` on my Linux desktop.

I also confirmed that these changes do indeed fix the bug in all 5 of those MRPs, pretty much confirming they are all this issue.
Seems like the same fix as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104501

> Seems like the same fix as #104501

Wow, yep it's the same thing. I'm not sure how I didn't come across that in my searches, I guess probably because no one had made the connection and linked any of the issues to it.

I do think my version with `std::byte` and `reinterpret_cast` is a little more expressive, and that we should still revert the "Do not inline `new` operators" change, but that PR includes fixing `hash_murmur3_buffer` as well as proactively changing the behavior of _setup not to hash trailing bytes if `sizeof(Data)` were ever changed to not be a multiple of 4.

I cherry-picked @corngood's additional changes to make sure David's authorship is included, and merged them in so they match the current codebase (filenames have changed since April 2025, so the #104501 can't be trivially merged directly). I also re-ran all 5 of the MRPs from the linked issues and verified it's all still working with the new commit.

I did a little git archaeology and found that the hashing done in `_setup` here predates `hash_murmur3_buffer` (originally called `hash_murmur3_32`) by about 2 years, so I imagine the only reason _setup isn't just doing a simple `h = hash_murmur3_buffer(p_base_ptr, p_ptr_size);` is that the function wasn't available when it was written, and no one has cared to go back and replace it.

I'd be happy to replace the hash `_setup` is doing with a call to `hash_murmur3_buffer` now that `hash_murmur3_buffer` is fixed thanks to @corngood. Doing so was briefly mentioned in #104501 but I don't see any discussion of why it wasn't done. As far as I can tell the pro is not having mostly redundant hashing code in callable_mp.cpp, the con is that the hashes it generates are subtly different, so it does mean a small behavior change beyond just fixing the aliasing/LTO bug. I can't imagine changing the hash would cause any problems (it was changed from djb2 to murmur3 back in 2022, seemingly without issue aside from this aliasing bug).  I've confirmed the test suite all passes and verified those same 5 MRPs are still fixed after switching `_setup` to use the fixed `hash_murmur3_buffer`, but I'll defer to a maintainer whether you'd prefer the minimal fix (the current PR), or whether you'd like me to push this change swapping it out for a call to `hash_murmur3_buffer`.
